The main takeaway from our work is that
gas transport efficacy in the four construction principles is determined by the same functional principles and the same limitations, and that the differences in efficacy are not very pronounced.

, although the gas exchange performance of different systems is determined by the construction principles, the actual efficiency attained is determined by the relative magnitudes of ventilation, medium/blood transfer, and perfusion, and by the relative magnitude of the driving force of gas transfer.
, although the construction of respiratory organs may vary widely between species, the principles of respiratory gas exchange in vertebrate species are surprisingly similar.
